summary: A small reviewed library of transferable product-interface principles with explicit provenance, limits, freshness, and originality constraints.

records.title: Developer Platforms
records.purpose: Keep dense technical work direct, legible, and efficient.

positiveSignals: The Task changes a repeated technical workflow on a rendered product surface.
negativeSignals: The Task is backend-only, generated-only, documentation-only, or a public page.

records.problem: Equal-weight panels and decorative containers can hide the primary technical object.
records.guidance: Center one technical work object; keep active orientation, scope, freshness, decisive change, evidence, action, and recovery visible while secondary metadata recedes progressively.
failureModes: Copying a recognizable developer-tool shell or mistaking compact dark styling for expert usability.

accessibility: Preserve semantic order, keyboard access, focus visibility, and readable density.
trust: Keep status, scope, and destructive consequences visible.
responsive: Move secondary inspectors into named surfaces before compressing the primary work.
originality: Do not copy another product's shell, palette, grid, navigation, copy, or assets.

records.operationalCost: Requires overflow, focus-order, and pane-state proof.

records.title: AI-Assisted Products
records.purpose: Make automated help understandable, steerable, and recoverable.

positiveSignals: The rendered workflow generates, recommends, delegates, remembers, or acts with AI.
negativeSignals: AI is an implementation detail with no user-visible state, choice, or consequence.

records.problem: Opaque capability, memory, or authority encourages overreliance and makes correction difficult.
records.guidance: Show the AI goal, accessible scope, included and excluded sources, uncertainty, current stage, and external effect; preserve user state and keep correction, rejection, and reversal easy.
failureModes: Anthropomorphic certainty, invisible memory, or autonomous action without meaningful control.

accessibility: Communicate AI state and changes through text and semantics, not animation or color alone.
trust: Expose scope, permissions, uncertainty, consequences, and recovery in proportion to risk.
responsive: Keep the current task and control path reachable when supporting reasoning moves into a secondary surface.
originality: Do not copy branded AI symbols, agent personas, reasoning layouts, or company-specific language.

records.operationalCost: Requires state, permission, interruption, error, and reversal proof.

records.title: Commerce Operations
records.purpose: Help operators act quickly without losing business context or control.

positiveSignals: The Task changes merchant, catalog, order, inventory, fulfillment, or business operations.
negativeSignals: The surface is a public storefront or marketing page rather than an operational product workflow.

records.problem: Duplicated content, jargon, and disconnected actions slow global operators and increase mistakes.
records.guidance: Keep the current merchant object and business consequence visible; preserve validated data, use consistent terms, show interruption and progress truthfully, and make the next recoverable action explicit.
failureModes: Repeating the same content across containers or hiding business consequences behind generic labels.

accessibility: Use semantic structure, short scannable content, and non-color state cues.
trust: State affected objects, quantities, timing, and recovery before consequential actions.
responsive: Preserve the primary business object and action while secondary context transforms.
originality: Do not copy Shopify or Stripe Admin conventions outside their platforms.

records.operationalCost: Requires terminology, locale, consequence, and recovery review.

records.title: Financial And High-Trust Products
records.purpose: Make consequential decisions calm, explicit, and reviewable.

positiveSignals: The Task presents money, authorization, compliance, identity, or another consequential decision.
negativeSignals: The rendered surface carries no consequential or sensitive state.

records.problem: Visual novelty can obscure amount, party, timing, permission, confidence, or reversibility.
records.guidance: Before action, isolate the proposed change and money-moving consequence, limit, requester, independent verification, duration or revocation, and audit result; favor legible confidence over ornament.
failureModes: Weak contrast, ambiguous totals, hidden permissions, or dramatic motion around irreversible actions.

accessibility: Do not use color alone for money, risk, identity, or completion state.
trust: State actor, amount or object, destination, timing, permission, and recovery before confirmation.
responsive: Keep review facts adjacent to confirmation at every width.
originality: Do not borrow financial brands, branded components, copy, illustrations, or trust marks.

records.operationalCost: Requires consequence, error, permission, and audit-state proof.

records.title: Application Workbench
records.purpose: Orient repeated work around one primary object and next decision.

positiveSignals: The Task changes a multi-region workspace used for repeated operational work.
negativeSignals: The Task is a short linear flow or public page.

records.problem: Equal-weight regions make work compete with navigation, filters, and metadata.
records.guidance: Keep the primary object central, active orientation stable but quiet, and health, evidence, state, and actions beside rather than over the work; preserve those roles when panes recompose.
failureModes: Carding every region, duplicating headers, or making inspectors block the task without reason.

accessibility: Keep landmarks, pane labels, focus order, and return focus stable.
trust: Preserve visible status and unsaved work through navigation.
responsive: Assign one scroll owner and transform secondary panes into named drawers or routes.
originality: Adapt the structure to project components rather than copying a workbench shell.

records.operationalCost: Requires keyboard, overflow, scroll-owner, and pane-state proof.

records.title: Setup And Onboarding
records.purpose: Get a person to a meaningful first outcome with clear choices and recovery.

positiveSignals: The Task introduces, configures, connects, imports, or activates a product capability.
negativeSignals: The user already has context and performs the workflow repeatedly.

records.problem: Feature tours and premature configuration delay value and hide required decisions.
records.guidance: Explain the immediate outcome, preserved information, current step, necessary permission, and next action; show interruption, retry, progress, and first confirmation truthfully while deferring optional setup.
failureModes: Long tours, unexplained permissions, irreversible defaults, or celebratory screens before success.

accessibility: Use headings, steps, labels, and errors that remain understandable without visual decoration.
trust: Explain permissions, data use, defaults, and reversibility before commitment.
responsive: Transform supporting explanation without separating a choice from its consequence.
originality: Use project language and product facts; do not imitate another product's setup sequence.

records.operationalCost: Requires first-run, validation, skip, resume, and failure proof.

records.title: Review, Approval, Or Transaction
records.purpose: Support an informed consequential decision without distraction.

positiveSignals: The Task confirms, approves, pays, publishes, deletes, grants, or submits a consequential change.
negativeSignals: The action is immediate, trivial, and safely reversible.

records.problem: Generic confirmation UI can omit the exact object, change, authority, or recovery path.
records.guidance: Place the exact before-and-after difference, decisive evidence, consequence, and recovery before the action; name the outcome with a verb and separate review from execution when risk warrants it.
failureModes: Vague confirm labels, hidden changes, accidental double action, or success without an audit trail.

accessibility: Announce errors and completion, preserve focus, and offer a non-color review of changes.
trust: Show actor, object, change, destination, timing, and reversibility before execution.
responsive: Keep decisive facts and the final action in the same reading path.
originality: Do not copy branded payment, approval, or security treatments.

records.operationalCost: Requires double-submit, error, reversal, and audit-state proof.

records.title: Monitoring And Operational Status
records.purpose: Make current health, meaningful change, and next action scannable.

positiveSignals: The Task shows ongoing system, deployment, queue, incident, or operational state.
negativeSignals: The surface is a static report with no changing state or operational response.

records.problem: Dense dashboards can give every metric urgency while hiding freshness and causal context.
records.guidance: Lead with health, freshness, affected scope, and meaningful change; connect chronology to ownership, recovery, and follow-up while disclosing raw detail on demand.
failureModes: Vanity metrics, constant red urgency, stale status without timestamps, or charts without decisions.

accessibility: Pair visual encodings with text and ensure tables or summaries preserve the same meaning.
trust: Show freshness, source, scope, uncertainty, and degraded-data states.
responsive: Prioritize health and action; move historical or diagnostic detail behind explicit navigation.
originality: Do not copy another platform's observability shell, chart palette, or status vocabulary.

records.operationalCost: Requires live, stale, partial, empty, alert, and recovery proof.

records.title: AI-Assisted Or Delegated Work
records.purpose: Keep a person oriented and in control while automation helps or acts.

positiveSignals: The Task asks AI to generate, recommend, remember, coordinate, or take action.
negativeSignals: There is no user-visible AI capability, state, or delegation.

records.problem: A chat-like surface alone does not explain working scope, progress, evidence, or authority.
records.guidance: Keep goal, bounded scope, source evidence, uncertainty, and current stage visible; separate proposal from action and provide inspect, correct, pause, reject, approve, and reverse in proportion to risk.
failureModes: False familiarity, hidden tools or memory, vague progress, and irreversible delegated action.

accessibility: Make generated changes, progress, and controls available without relying on animation or spatial position.
trust: State capabilities, data scope, permissions, uncertainty, and irreversible boundaries.
responsive: Preserve the goal, current action, and intervention controls while reasoning detail moves elsewhere.
originality: Do not copy branded assistant personas, thread chrome, agent icons, or reasoning presentation.

records.operationalCost: Requires capability, permission, interruption, correction, error, and recovery proof.

records.title: Mobile Task Transformation
records.purpose: Preserve the task when space, input, attention, and environment change.

positiveSignals: The Task must work across compact, medium, and expanded layouts or touch-first contexts.
negativeSignals: The product has an explicit, truthful desktop-only constraint.

records.problem: Shrinking desktop regions creates tiny controls, nested scroll, hidden state, and broken reading order.
records.guidance: Recompose around the primary task, sequence evidence before action, preserve state and recovery, use platform-appropriate controls, and keep fixed or sticky regions from obscuring content.
failureModes: Compressed multi-column layouts, unexplained icon-only actions, or destructive controls detached from context.

accessibility: Maintain target size, reading order, zoom, focus, and reduced-motion behavior.
trust: Do not hide state, consequence, or limitations to fit a narrow surface.
responsive: Transform regions and navigation deliberately rather than scaling the desktop composition.
originality: Do not reproduce platform materials or expressive components unless project authority adopts them.

records.operationalCost: Requires narrow, intermediate, wide, touch, keyboard, and orientation proof.

records.title: Evidence Before Reduction
records.purpose: Prevent simplification from deleting required context, states, and recovery.

positiveSignals: The Task creates or materially revises a rendered workflow with decisions, state, evidence, or recovery.
negativeSignals: The Task is a purely decorative adjustment with no product-state or interaction obligation.

records.problem: Agents may trade required evidence and interaction for a quiet happy path.
records.guidance: Before simplifying, preserve every task-required object, orientation cue, decisive fact, state, action, error, and recovery; render meaningful default content before enhancement and make interactions real at each required viewport.
failureModes: Missing orientation, decisive facts, real actions, visible failures, or recovery.

accessibility: Keep required states and actions perceivable and operable.
trust: Keep consequence, authority, freshness, and recovery visible.
responsive: Keep evidence before action and do not obscure required content.

records.operationalCost: Requires visible-state, interaction, recovery, and equivalent cross-viewport proof.

records.title: Quiet Structural Hierarchy
records.purpose: Let structure support the work without making every boundary visible.

positiveSignals: A dense interface gives navigation, containers, and content equal visual weight.
negativeSignals: The project design system requires stronger separation for accessibility or brand reasons.

records.problem: Borders, cards, labels, icons, and accent color on every region create noise rather than hierarchy.
records.guidance: Prefer alignment, spacing, typography, and restrained layers before adding containers or accent color.
failureModes: Removing necessary boundaries or using low contrast in pursuit of visual quiet.

accessibility: Quiet hierarchy must retain perceivable grouping, contrast, and focus.
trust: Do not visually mute risk, status, or consequence.
responsive: Recompose hierarchy instead of erasing labels or context.
originality: Do not imitate a named product's minimal shell or monochrome palette.

records.operationalCost: Requires rendered hierarchy and contrast review.

records.title: Visible Automation Authority
records.purpose: Make the boundary between suggestion and action explicit.

positiveSignals: Automation can access data, remember context, or affect external state.
negativeSignals: The capability only formats local content with no sensitive data or external effect.

records.problem: People cannot calibrate trust when access, memory, permissions, and action rights are invisible.
records.guidance: Expose relevant scope and permission at the decision point, distinguish preview from execution, and keep rejection or reversal available.
failureModes: Overloaded consent, hidden memory, or treating a loading animation as adequate progress and control.

accessibility: State authority and outcomes in programmatically determinable text.
trust: Scale approval, audit, and reversal to consequence.
responsive: Keep intervention controls adjacent to the current automated action.
originality: Do not copy branded agent identity, consent wording, or reasoning UI.

records.operationalCost: Requires permission, preview, reject, reverse, and audit proof.

records.title: Adaptive Task Layout
records.purpose: Change composition with available space while preserving task meaning.

positiveSignals: The same workflow must remain usable across materially different widths or input modes.
negativeSignals: The Task targets one fixed and documented environment.

records.problem: Breakpoint scaling alone preserves the wrong simultaneous regions and interaction assumptions.
records.guidance: Start from the task and transform pane, rail, sheet, route, or sequence roles according to space and ergonomics.
failureModes: Using a fashionable component or platform material without project fit or implementation support.

accessibility: Preserve semantics, focus, targets, and state across transformations.
trust: Keep limitations and consequences visible in every composition.
responsive: Test compact, intermediate, and expanded behavior rather than only two screenshots.
originality: Do not copy Material, Apple, Stripe, or Vercel component styling.

records.operationalCost: Requires cross-breakpoint behavior and state-continuity proof.

sourceNotes.title: Linear 2026 Interface Refresh
sourceNotes.observation: Linear describes reducing equal visual weight, excessive icons, and visible treatments so the central task stays in focus while orientation recedes.
sourceNotes.transferRationale: The hierarchy principle transfers to dense repeated work when project evidence supports it.
limitations: A branded product retrospective is not a universal usability standard.
The source does not prove suitability for novice or high-risk workflows.
sourceNotes.licenseOrAssetRestrictions: Principles are paraphrased; no screenshots, copy, code, tokens, or assets are redistributed.

sourceNotes.title: Vercel Geist
sourceNotes.relevantSurface: Developer interfaces, layout, typography, components, and contextual panels
sourceNotes.observation: Geist documents a consistent high-contrast system and distinguishes persistent associated context from blocking decisions, with explicit keyboard and focus behavior.
sourceNotes.transferRationale: Semantic component choice, consistent foundations, and contextual detail patterns transfer when implemented through project-owned components.
limitations: Component advice reflects Vercel's system and implementation constraints.
Its aesthetic is not evidence of fit for another product.
sourceNotes.licenseOrAssetRestrictions: No component code, fonts, icons, screenshots, or brand assets are redistributed.

sourceNotes.title: Atlassian AI Interaction Guidelines
sourceNotes.observation: The guidance emphasizes contextual proactivity, flow preservation, inspectability, collaboration, permissions, risk communication, and course correction.
sourceNotes.transferRationale: These interaction responsibilities transfer to visible AI capabilities independently of Atlassian's brand expression.
limitations: Examples are shaped by Atlassian products and policies.
Specific disclosure or approval requirements remain project and jurisdiction dependent.
sourceNotes.licenseOrAssetRestrictions: Only original paraphrased principles are retained; no visual or textual assets are copied.

sourceNotes.title: Microsoft Fluent Responsible AI
sourceNotes.relevantSurface: AI transparency, scope, control, memory, permissions, errors, and recovery
sourceNotes.observation: The guidance covers expectation setting, source and accuracy cues, data and memory scope, meaningful latency, action rights, approval, correction, reversal, and actionable errors.
sourceNotes.transferRationale: Trust calibration and control principles transfer to AI interfaces, while policy details stay project-owned.
limitations: Some requirements are Microsoft product rules rather than general standards.
Displaying reasoning can introduce privacy, safety, or misinterpretation risks.
sourceNotes.licenseOrAssetRestrictions: No Fluent assets, components, screenshots, or exact copy are redistributed.

sourceNotes.title: Stripe Apps Design
sourceNotes.relevantSurface: Contextual financial operations and focused workflows
sourceNotes.observation: Stripe limits customization for consistency and accessibility, recommends meeting users in existing object context, and separates contextual side-by-side work from focused uninterrupted tasks.
sourceNotes.transferRationale: Context-first entry, appropriate focus, and constrained expression transfer to high-trust embedded workflows.
limitations: Direct component and surface rules apply only inside Stripe Apps.
Constrained customization is not automatically right for standalone products.
sourceNotes.licenseOrAssetRestrictions: No Stripe components, code, screenshots, copy, or brand assets are redistributed.

sourceNotes.title: Wise Design
sourceNotes.relevantSurface: Cross-platform financial brand and product consistency
sourceNotes.observation: Wise presents one design system spanning brand and product, supported by platform-specific tokens, components, patterns, and screen templates.
sourceNotes.transferRationale: A coherent authority with platform-specific implementations supports consistency without forcing identical composition.
limitations: The available source is an overview, not evidence for individual financial interaction patterns.
Wise brand expression is not transferable.
sourceNotes.licenseOrAssetRestrictions: No Wise assets, libraries, templates, screenshots, or copy are redistributed.

sourceNotes.title: Shopify App Content Guidance
sourceNotes.observation: Shopify recommends plain scannable language, consistent terminology, strong action verbs, prioritized steps, reduced duplication, and merchant control.
sourceNotes.transferRationale: Clear, consistent, action-oriented product language transfers to operational products with diverse users.
limitations: A grade-level benchmark is locale-specific and not a substitute for user research.
Shopify Admin conventions apply directly only to Shopify integrations.
sourceNotes.licenseOrAssetRestrictions: Only paraphrased writing principles are retained; no examples, images, or exact copy are redistributed.

sourceNotes.title: Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Materials
sourceNotes.relevantSurface: Platform hierarchy, materials, contrast, and context
sourceNotes.observation: Apple describes materials as hierarchy and orientation tools, separates functional controls from content, and recommends sparse use with legibility and system adaptation.
sourceNotes.transferRationale: Semantic layering, restraint, and context preservation transfer; platform material appearance does not.
limitations: Liquid Glass is platform-specific and can become visual noise or reduce contrast when generalized.
System components and accessibility settings change actual behavior.
sourceNotes.licenseOrAssetRestrictions: No Apple design resources, assets, screenshots, code, or platform appearance are redistributed.

sourceNotes.title: Material Design 3 Adaptive Layouts And States
sourceNotes.relevantSurface: Adaptive pane composition and interaction states
sourceNotes.observation: Material documents feed, list-detail, and supporting-pane scaffolds across compact, medium, and expanded breakpoints, plus consistent visible interaction states.
sourceNotes.transferRationale: Task-based pane transformation and complete states transfer when expressed through the project's system.
limitations: Canonical layouts are starting points, not universal solutions.
Material components and expressive styling should not overwrite a non-Material system.
sourceNotes.licenseOrAssetRestrictions: No Material kit, code, icons, screenshots, components, or exact styling are redistributed.

sourceNotes.title: GOV.UK Design System Accessibility Strategy
sourceNotes.relevantSurface: Universal design, progressive enhancement, evidence, and accessibility verification
sourceNotes.observation: The strategy emphasizes tolerance for error, low cognitive effort, semantic HTML, resilient fallbacks, evidenced prioritization, and combined automated, manual, and user research.
sourceNotes.transferRationale: Resilience and evidence-backed accessibility transfer across product domains and constrain visual trends.
limitations: Public-service priorities and governance do not map directly to every commercial product.
Automated checks alone cannot establish accessibility.
sourceNotes.licenseOrAssetRestrictions: No GOV.UK components, templates, screenshots, or exact content are redistributed.
